title: Inhabitants of any area are modified colonists from the most accessible source

fields.label: Label
fields.value: Inhabitants of any area are modified colonists from the most accessible source

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: The inhabitants of any area (oceanic islands, mountains, lakes, marshes, caves), where not identical, are plainly related to those of the region from which colonists could most readily have come, the colonists having since been modified and better fitted to their new homes.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: On the Origin of Species by Means of Natural Selection, or the Preservation of Favoured Races in the Struggle for Life

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: The principle which determines the general character of the fauna and flora of oceanic islands, namely, that the inhabitants, when not identically the same, yet are plainly related to the inhabitants of that region whence colonists could most readily have been derived,—the colonists having been subsequently modified and better fitted to their new homes,—is of the widest application throughout nature.

fields.label: Agent
fields.value: delphisci Origin of Species claim extractor

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Charles Darwin, On the Origin of Species (1st ed., London: John Murray, 1859), Chapter XII, “Geographical Distribution, continued”; section “On colonisation from the nearest source with subsequent modification”. Scope: biotas of islands, mountains, lakes, marshes and caves

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on darwin1859-ch12-15: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.64

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Modern phylogeography can test many examples, but no harmonized dataset spans all listed environments and taxa. Historical-source inference and evidence of subsequent adaptation remain confounded and specialist-intensive.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Infer source regions for insular, montane, aquatic, marsh and cave lineages from dated phylogenies and ancestral ranges, then compare inferred sources with quantified dispersal accessibility and test for post-colonization trait shifts. Concordant accessible sources and derived local adaptations support the claim.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Accessibility is lineage- and time-dependent and requires substantial interpretation.

Adaptation to the new home is not directly recorded for most lineages.

Extinction and range shifts can erase source populations.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
data existence: 0.82
analysis feasibility: 0.58
data adequacy: 0.55
operationalizability: 0.62
discriminating power: 0.55

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: The colonisation half can be turned into a source-region test, but accessibility and subsequent adaptation each admit several operationalizations, which lowers the score. Phylogenies and range data cover classic islands much better than caves, marshes and alpine lakes. A broad multi-habitat analysis would take months of harmonization, and adaptation remains a proxy rather than a fitness measurement.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: For islands, sky-islands, lakes and caves, compare the phylogenetic source region of endemics with a dispersal-accessibility model based on distance and barriers, and score whether colonists are phenotypically shifted toward local conditions. The claim is confirmed if the best-supported source matches the most accessible region and derived populations are more environment-matched than their source relatives, and refuted if sources are random with respect to access or phenotypes are unchanged.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Cave, marsh and lake endemics are inventoried far more unevenly than oceanic islands.

Being related to a source shows colonisation, while 'better fitted' needs trait-environment data that most of these biotas lack.

'Most readily' requires a dispersal model, and currents, bird vectors and past climates give several competing versions.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
discriminating power: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.45
data existence: 0.7
operationalizability: 0.55
data adequacy: 0.45
